newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman Raysut port in $45mln deal for gantry cranes.
newsitem.headline: Oman Raysut port in $45mln deal for gantry cranes.

text.p: The Omani government and Oman's Salalah Port Services Co (SPS) on Monday signed two contracts worth a total $45 million to buy 18 gantry cranes for its port of Mina Raysut from Japan and China, an SPS statement said.
The statement said the first agreement with Japan's Ishikawjima-Harima Heavy Industries Co Ltd was for six quay-side gantry cranes.
A second agreement was signed with a Chinese company identified only as Z.P.M.C for 12 rubber-tyred gantry cranes.
The statement did not give a breakdown of the value of each contract but said that the equipment would be supplied to site by July 1998.
"Additional purchases of up to $70 million are planned based on throughput requirements," it said.

"This will include six more quay-side gantry cranes, 12 rubber tyred gantry cranes, up to 100 tractors and trailers, several forklifts and a modern computerised container handling system to support yard and vessel operations," it added.
SPS founder shareholders are the Omani government, CSX Corp's Sea-Land Services Inc, local firms and pension funds. SPS said on Monday Maersk had acquired a 15 percent stake in the company.
Oman hopes Raysut port will establish it as a gateway for container traffic in the Gulf, east Africa and India.
